Sources & assumptions

Version 1.9 · Medical sources checked November 18, 2026. General US household planning, not live alerts or address-level hazard assessment.

Experience and supply goals

Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced change the depth of guidance. Core, Advanced and Super prep set 3, 14 or 30 days. These choices are independent.

Water

Water = (adults + children + infants) × gallons/person/day × days + pets × entered gallons/pet/day × days. The baseline is 1 gallon/person/day. Beginner mode adds a visible half-gallon/person/day starter buffer when extreme heat or extra needs are selected, and rounds the shopping list up to whole one-gallon jugs. This editorial buffer is not an individualized medical or heat-safety requirement. Intermediate/Advanced use the entered daily allowance. Pets need species- and situation-specific amounts; the 0.25-gallon default is only a placeholder.

Food

Beginner mode asks for complete household days of familiar meals and normal portions. It does not require calorie counting. Intermediate/Advanced food = (adults × adult daily calories + children × child daily calories) × days. Defaults of 2,000 adult and 1,600 child calories are editable inventory placeholders, not prescriptions. Infant feeding is separate. The two inventory methods remain separate when switching experience; no automatic conversion is made. Meals = 3 × days × people eating solid food. Package servings are not necessarily meals.

Power

Beginner mode starts with personal lights, cables and one tested USB bank around 20,000 mAh per entered phone. Actual phone charges vary; test each pairing. This is not a promise of power for the selected duration. Longer outages need safe recurring recharging or relocation. Medical equipment needs a device-specific professional plan.

Detailed calculator: nominal battery Wh = daily Wh × days ÷ usable fraction. Runtime = battery Wh × usable fraction ÷ daily Wh. No recharge is assumed. Output watts, surge, device compatibility and environmental losses require separate checks. The 90 Wh/day example represents 50 Wh of lights plus 40 Wh of phone charging, not measured household consumption.

Portable power uses measured Wh/day when supplied, or rated watts multiplied by full-power-equivalent hours per day. No-sun battery target = Wh/day × backup hours ÷ 24 ÷ usable fraction. Solar estimate = the lower of panel watts and the entered station limit × equivalent peak sun hours × yield fraction. If the input limit is blank, panel watts are used with a reminder to verify the station. These are planning estimates. Verify device startup, standby, actual test runtime and weather-dependent recharging.

Communications

AM/FM and NOAA receivers receive information; they do not send a help request. NOAA weather tuning alone is not automatic alerting. Voice radio, mesh text and satellite systems have different equipment, licensing, coverage and service requirements. No advertised range or map dot proves your route. Test both ends and retain a paper fallback. Mesh tests should disable internet/MQTT bridges while retaining needed local phone-to-radio connections.

Medical preparedness

Medical depth follows experience. Beginner provides essential supplies, Intermediate adds Advanced medical planning, and Advanced adds Expert medical planning. OTC quantities are starter shopping allowances, not dosing schedules. Clinicians authorize prescription reserves and standby kits. Medical inventory is optional, with independent opt-ins for browser saving and export inclusion. Dates create reminders when the page is open. Prices were checked against provider/manufacturer pages on November 18, 2026; other ranges are editorial budget allowances. Individual eligibility, licensing and final prescriptions require verification by the patient and provider.

Privacy and limits

Checklist progress is done tasks divided by applicable tasks. Items marked Not needed are excluded and appear in the final PDF with their status. Regional presets are editorial prompts; town/state is a label only. Plans are stored in your browser, with no application database or analytics. Hosting infrastructure may receive ordinary request metadata. Keep exports private. No service worker is installed: a hosted page is not guaranteed offline. Download the guides, print a plan or keep the source bundle locally.
